# oxframe

oxframe is procedural animation in Rust. Scenes are async functions; awaiting an animation takes time.

Full text: https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/llms-full.txt

## Start here

- [Welcome](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0): Learn oxframe: make animations and motion graphics by writing Rust code, with a live editor to scrub through them and fine-tune the timing.
- [Install and first project](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/getting-started): Install the oxframe CLI with cargo, create your first animation project and open the live editor — five minutes from nothing to a moving scene.

## Guide

- [1. Your first animation](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/hello): Lesson 1 of the oxframe guide: add a circle to the screen and animate it with Rust. The basic pattern behind every animation, with a live example.
- [2. In order, or all at once](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/together): Lesson 2: run animations in order, all at once or as a ripple with all and stagger, plus ready-made entrances like fade_in and pop_in.
- [3. Shapes, colors, transforms](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/shapes): Lesson 3: rectangles, circles, lines and polygons; fills and outlines; rotation, scale and color — the properties every oxframe shape shares.
- [4. Easing](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/easing): Lesson 4: easing curves explained — why some animations feel natural and others robotic, and how to pick the right ease-in and ease-out curve.
- [5. Text](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/text): Lesson 5: animate text in Rust — titles, typewriter effects, mixed styles and syntax-highlighted code blocks with oxframe.
- [6. Groups and layout](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/groups): Lesson 6: nest shapes in groups and let flexbox-style layout arrange them, so whole compositions move and scale together.
- [7. Tweak timing in the editor](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/editor): Lesson 7: adjust timing by eye in the oxframe editor — markers, eases and tunables you can drag without touching or recompiling code.
- [8. Signals](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/signals): Lesson 8: signals make one value follow another — a line that always connects two dots, a label that always shows a number.
- [9. Drawing and morphing](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/drawing): Lesson 9: draw an outline as if with a pen, then morph one shape into another — path drawing and shape morphing in oxframe.
- [10. Randomness and background tasks](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/random): Lesson 10: background tasks and seeded randomness — many things moving on their own while the story continues, rendering the same video every time.
- [11. Scenes and transitions](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/scenes): Lesson 11: build a video from several scenes and blend them with slide, fade, wipe and zoom transitions, all in one oxframe render.
- [12. Sound and voice](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/sound): Lesson 12: add sound effects on the beat, a soundtrack that ducks under speech, and time animations to the words of a spoken line.
- [13. Shaders and effects](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/shaders): Lesson 13: animated water, drops on the camera lens, ripples on a node and a water transition — shader presets you animate like any property.
- [14. Charts and graphs](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/charts): Lesson 14: plot functions on axes, ride a dot along a curve, morph it into another function and zoom — the whole chart follows the ranges.
- [15. Vectors and matrices](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/matrices): Lesson 15: draw a vector on axes, stretch the whole plane with a 2 × 2 matrix and show the numbers in brackets — the grid and the arrow follow.

## Going further

- [Components](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/guide/components): Build an explainer from ready-made blocks: title cards, bullet lists, code, flow diagrams, callouts, lower thirds and end cards.
- [All nodes](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/nodes): Reference of every oxframe node and its properties: Rect, Circle, Line, Path, Polygon, Star, Txt, Code, Img, Layout and Grid.
- [Effects](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/effects): Gradients, dashes, shadows, blur, blend modes and clipping in oxframe. Every effect is a signal and animates like any other property.
- [Animated charts and plots](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/charts): Animated charts in Rust: axes with labels, function plots that follow animated ranges, bars that grow with their values, and number lines.
- [Matrices, vectors and tables](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/matrices): Animated matrices, vectors and tables in Rust: matrix multiplication step by step, linear maps that bend the grid, and rows that sort themselves.
- [Writing your own node](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/custom-nodes): Make a node of your own in Rust: a struct that draws with DrawCtx, animatable signal fields, layout and checks, and a crate template.
- [Icons: Lucide, Tabler and brand logos](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/icons): Lucide, Tabler and Simple Icons in Rust animations: icon!("lucide:server") by name, colors and line widths as signals, and icons in flow diagrams.
- [Camera](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/camera): Zoom, pan and rotate the view in oxframe: fit a whole diagram, center on a detail, follow a moving node, and keep titles on screen.
- [Markers, eases, tunables](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/timing): Markers, custom eases and tunables: timing values stored outside your Rust code so you can adjust them visually in the oxframe editor.
- [The editor](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/editor): A tour of the oxframe editor: viewport, timeline, inspector and hot reload — the same app in oxframe dev and in the browser playground.
- [Rendering video](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/rendering): Render oxframe animations to MP4, WebM with alpha, ProRes 4444 or PNG sequences with one command, on the GPU or CPU, with audio and scene transitions.
- [CLI reference](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/cli): Reference for the oxframe command line: init, dev, render, snapshot, check, agents, upgrade and mcp, with all options.
- [Working with AI agents](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/agents): Use Claude Code, Codex or Cursor to write oxframe animations: every project ships agent instructions and a way for agents to see what they made.

## Under the hood

- [How oxframe works](https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.17.0/how-it-works): How oxframe works inside: scenes as Rust coroutines, deterministic rendering, instant scrubbing, and compiling Rust to WebAssembly for the browser.
